_note: Bean-size grades the Price Check photo can estimate, and how each maps to Tanzania Coffee Board auction grades for pricing. Size bands are from EAS 130:1999. The photo-class -> auction-grade mapping is OUR choice (rationale in docs/PRICING.md), not an official rule.

size_standard.source: East African Standard EAS 130:1999 'Green coffee beans - Specification', Table 1 'Coffee grades by size' (screens per ISO 4150; round holes for flat beans, slotted for peaberries)
size_standard.rule: When a coffee grade is specified, a minimum 95 % of the beans shall fall in that grade category (EAS 130 clause 5.1).

size_bands_mm.eas: Retained on 21 (8,3 mm); two beans joined / very large
Flat beans, through 21 retained on 18 (7,2 mm)
Flat beans, through 18 retained on 16 (6,35 mm)
Smaller beans, through 16 retained on 10 (3,96 mm)
Smallest, brokens; through screen 7 (2,9 mm). Gap 2.9-3.96 mm assigned to T by us.

peaberry.eas: Peaberries, through 17 retained on 12 (4,76 mm), slotted screen. Detected by shape (classifier), not width.

moisture_max_percent.eas: EAS 130 clause 4.2.1: moisture content maximum 10,5 % (m/m). The photo cannot measure this.

damage_classes.eas: EAS 130 clause 4.2.3: classes 1-6 free from damage; class 7 damage up to 5 %; class 8 up to 15 %; class 9 up to 25 %; class 10 up to 60 % of beans.
